---
title: "Modèle non linéaire paramétrique"
output: html_document
date: "2025-09-30"
---

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
# -------------------------------
# 1. Simulation des données sous un modèle logistique
# -------------------------------
doses <- c(0, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 5, 10)
n_per <- 10 # même nb d'échantillons pour chaque groupe
# vrai paramètres du modèle
beta0 <- -2 
beta1 <- 0.8

dat <- expand.grid(dose = doses, rep = 1:n_per) %>%
  mutate(
    eta = beta0 + beta1 * dose,
    p = plogis(eta),
    Y = rbinom(n(), 1, p)
  ) %>%
  mutate(dose_f = factor(dose, levels = doses))

```

```{r}
# -------------------------------
# 2. Ajustement linéaire et logistique
# -------------------------------
fit_lin <- lm(Y ~ dose, data = dat)
fit_log <- glm(Y ~ dose, family = binomial, data = dat)

# prédictions
grid <- data.frame(dose = seq(min(doses), max(doses), length.out = 200))
grid$pred_lin <- predict(fit_lin, newdata = grid)
grid$pred_log <- predict(fit_log, newdata = grid, type = "response")


fit_log

# -------------------------------
# 3. Visualisation
# -------------------------------
ggplot(dat, aes(x = dose, y = Y)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.05, width = 0.1, alpha = 0.5) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3, color = "black") +
  geom_line(data = grid, aes(x = dose, y = pred_lin), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = grid, aes(x = dose, y = pred_log), color = "red", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Réponse binaire simulée",
       subtitle = "Rouge = modèle logistique (correct), Bleu = linéaire (mauvaise option)",
       y = "Probabilité d'effet") +
  theme_minimal()
```
